Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & evals

Hi John / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciate you walking us through the Acme requirements and the two MVP flows (customer support triage & internal knowledge search). Per our follow-up agreement, I pulled together a shortlist of model candidates with tradeoffs and links to the evals we ran against your prompt set. High-level recap below plus next steps.

Quick recap of what you shared:
- Primary outcome: accurate intent classification + concise, extractive answer generation for KB articles (targets: >92% intent accuracy, <250ms average token latency for generation).
- Hard constraints: PII redaction pipeline in front of calls, prefer self-hosted/private deployment for regulated data, cost target: <$0.005 per 1k tokens for generation where possible.

Recommended shortlist (rationale in parentheses):
1) Llama-3-8B (int8) — best latency/cost balance for extractive QA; strong on latency (<150ms) with our Dedicated offering; quality is near SOTA on short-context retrieval tasks. (Fast, cheap, good for high throughput.)
2) Mistral-7B Instruct (q4_0) — higher quality on instruction-following and hallucination reduction; slightly higher token cost and latency (~200-300ms). (Good if you prioritize answer quality over unit cost.)
3) Redmond-34B (fp16) — highest quality for long-form synthesis and edge cases, but significantly higher cost and latency; recommend as fallback for canary/critical flows only. (Quality-focused tier.)

Attached: Acme_MVP_eval_results.csv (benchmarks vs your prompt set), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (anonymized prompts we used), and the post-demo deck (summary + rollout suggestions). Links to the full benchmark dashboards are below.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm which of the three models you want us to run a 2-week eval on in your environment (Dedicated or Private).
- If Dedicated, we can provision a small reserved pool for the eval; if Private, we’ll share the install/air-gapped plan and checklist.
- We’ll run a focused regression suite (we flagged 23 edge prompts) and deliver a short quality report.

Would love your preference by EOD Thursday so we can schedule the evals next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Hi all — jumping in with the Ops/bench perspective.

Quick notes on cost/latency (numbers are approximate from our Dedicated baseline):
- Llama-3-8B (int8): ~0.9ms/token on A10-like instance; estimated unit cost ~ $0.0018 per 1k tokens on Dedicated if you use continuous batching and prefix caching. Avg gen latency for typical KB answers: 120–160ms.
- Mistral-7B (q4_0): ~1.6ms/token; estimated unit cost ~ $0.0028 per 1k tokens; avg gen latency: 200–320ms.
- Redmond-34B (fp16): ~5–8ms/token; estimated unit cost ~ $0.01+ per 1k tokens; avg gen latency: 450–900ms (depends on sequence length).

Operational comments:
- For the 2-week eval, recommend Dedicated small pool (2 GPUs) to hit representative throughput; it’s easiest for instrumentation and cost tracking.
- Private deploy: plan for a 2–3 day install window for a basic cluster (network, VPN/KMS, and firewall rules), plus an additional day for model weights sync and initial tests. We’ll need a point of contact from Acme infra for firewall/KMS work.
- We sanitized the prompt_set_v1.jsonl to remove PII, but flagged prompts that still contain customer examples — see column "flag_reason" in the CSV.

I’ll attach a short benchmark extract in the shared Drive for your review (link below).

—Jonas

Adding a quality/regression note from the Eval team side.

- We ran the prompt_set_v1 against the three candidates and produced the attached CSV. There are two regression patterns we observed with Llama-3-8B int8 versus Mistral-7B: 1) occasional omission of small entity values in extractive answers (~3% of cases), and 2) higher sensitivity to prompt phrasing for multi-step instructions. Both are addressable with prompt templates and controlled sampling, but we should include a focused regression test in the eval plan (we can run nightly difference reports).
- If Acme is sensitive to those omissions, our recommendation is to: start with Llama-3-8B for throughput, deploy deterministic decoding and an extractive post-check (simple regex/substring match), and run Mistral-7B in a canary route for high-risk queries.

Happy to hop on a quick session to walk through the CSV and the 23 flagged prompts.

—Rachel
